## Josh Allen

Allen is the best QB in the Stat Hub numbers: 26.8 half-PPR points per game over 7 games, and 23.5 over the last 4. Part of that is a rushing profile no other QB has. He averages 7.9 carries and 38.6 rush yards per game, with 9 rushing TDs, 17 red-zone carries and 10 goal-line carries. He plays 99% of snaps. The last 4 weeks are a little lower (6.8 carries, 3 rush TDs, 5 goal-line carries) but the usage is still elite. His passing is steady, not spectacular: 29.3 attempts and 256.1 yards per game, with 11 TDs against 5 INTs. He is Healthy, and my web search found nothing current for 2026. The results were all 2022 elbow news, so I can't confirm anything beyond the Healthy tag. His Week 8 line was 289 passing yards, 2 passing TDs and a rushing TD, with 30 rushing yards on seven carries.

The matchup is bad this week. Minnesota allows 7.8 half-PPR points per game to QBs against a league average of 16.5, the toughest QB matchup. That puts a ×0.80 on his number. The projection is 20.7 (experts 21.2, our model 19.8), with a range of 14.7 to 27.7. Even in a matchup this tough, his rushing keeps the floor above Maye's. Rest-of-season projection is 227.6, with a schedule ease of 0.98.

## Drake Maye

Maye has played 9 games and averages 19.9 points per game, 23.0 over the last 4. His passing volume is real: 30.2 attempts and 253.6 yards per game, with 18 TDs. The problem is turnovers. He has 11 INTs and 2 lost fumbles, and he threw 3 INTs against Green Bay on Sunday. His rushing is a smaller part of his value, and it's fading: 4.3 carries and 14.5 yards per game over the last 4 at 3.4 yards per carry. He has only 6 red-zone carries and 4 goal-line carries all season.

Teammates matter here. A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder) are still out, and Mack Hollins just returned from IR (calf). That is a thin receiving group, and Green Bay sacked Maye 4 times. I couldn't verify his injury status, since my search only returned 2024 and early 2026 items. He is listed Healthy.

This week he faces GB, the 7th toughest QB matchup (×0.91). The projection is 20.2 (experts 20.5), with a range of 8.2 to 24.6. That floor is the lowest of the two by a wide margin. Rest-of-season projection is 154.2 over fewer remaining games, well behind Allen's 227.6.

## The verdict

Allen wins both timeframes. Rest of season it isn't close: 227.6 projected against 154.2, backed by rushing and goal-line work that Maye doesn't have. This week the projections are nearly even (20.7 vs 20.2), but Allen's floor is much higher (14.7 vs 8.2). Maye's three-INT games and thin receiver group make him the riskier start. Start Allen despite the Minnesota matchup, since his rushing offsets it. If you own both, Maye is a fine bench QB or a trade chip, not a hold at Allen's price. Neither injury status is verified beyond the Healthy tags.
